thread.title: Nearly half of U.S. homes will have a smart speaker by year's end, Adobe says

author: morningstar.com
title: Nearly half of U.S. homes will have a smart speaker by year's end, Adobe says
text:
By Mike Murphy
Study finds users mostly like to listen to music
Turns out, we all just want someone who listens to us.
Or at least, some thing.
A new study released Monday found that American consumers have not grown tired of the novelty of voice-activated assistants -- in fact, such devices are already in about a third of U.S. homes, and that number is expected to reach nearly 50% by the end of the year.
Voice assistants, in the form of smart speakers such as Amazon.com's (AMZN) Echo, Alphabet's (GOOGL) (GOOGL) Google Home and Apple's (AAPL) HomePod, are now in 32% of homes, up from 28% in January, according to the report by Adobe Analytics (https://www.cmo.com/features/articles/2018/9/7/adobe-2018-consumer-voice-survey.html), a unit of Adobe Systems Inc. (ADBE) . And that's before the holiday shopping season, when analysts expect 79% of smart speakers to be sold this year. The report predicts 48% of households will have a smart speaker by the end of 2018.
"Technology trends come and go, but we think voice is here to stay," Colin Morris, director of product management for Adobe Analytics, said in a statement. "Consumers continue to embrace voice as a means to engage their devices and the internet. It's a trend that has fundamentally changed the face of computing."
Read:Your children have lessons to teach Alexa (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/what-your-children-can-teach-alexa-2018-08-09)
And what are we doing with our devices? Playing music and getting the weather forecast are the most common uses. Other popular activities include asking "fun questions," online searches and checking the news.
One segment that is lagging: shopping. The report found that while 43% of smart-speaker owners use the devices to make shopping lists, just 30% use them to order products.
Three-quarters of smart-speaker owners said they have increased their use of the devices over the past year; 71% said they talk to their device at least once a day, while 44% said they use it multiple times a day.
Owners of smart speakers are also product evangelists. The report found 45% of owners plan to buy another device for themselves, and 23% plan to buy one for someone else. And of those who do not own a smart speaker yet, almost a quarter say they plan to buy one for themselves.
-Mike Murphy; 1959ET
